subject_notes: Motion control across aerospace/defense platforms. Tier-2 supplier with broad PE-funding exposure.

claims.claim_text: Moog identifies the Lockheed Martin F-35 Lightning II as one of its named high-priority production programs, and the F-35 is a Military Aircraft segment production program. Backlog growth in Military Aircraft is attributed in part to the timing of F-35 orders.
claims.subject: F-35 Joint Strike Fighter
claims.object_value: F-35 program is a Military Aircraft production driver; backlog increase attributed to F-35 order timing
claims.source_quote: We maintain positions on numerous high priority programs, including the Lockheed Martin F-35 Lightning II. ... The twelve-month backlog in Military Aircraft increased due to the timing of orders for the F-35 program and new production programs.

claims.claim_text: Moog is currently working on development for the Textron Bell MV-75 (FLRAA / Future Long-Range Assault Aircraft) and attributes recent Military Aircraft sales growth in FY 2024 and FY 2025 to the MV-75 program ramp-up.
claims.subject: Textron Bell MV-75 (FLRAA)
claims.object_value: MV-75 cited as driver of $63M (2025) and $88M (2024) military OEM sales increases
claims.source_quote: Our military production programs include the F-35 Joint Strike Fighter and we are currently working on the development of the Textron Bell MV-75 and other classified funded development military programs. ... Sales increased in military OEM programs $63 million, driven by the ramp-up of activity on the MV-75 program and new production programs.

claims.claim_text: Moog's Space and Defense segment includes high-performance components/systems for space launch vehicles, satellites and spacecraft vehicles; FY 2024 gross margin gains were attributed to improved performance on space vehicle development programs.
claims.subject: Space launch / satellite / spacecraft programs
claims.object_value: Space launch + satellite + spacecraft programs cited as Space and Defense segment drivers
claims.source_quote: We also manufacture high-performance components and systems used for space launch vehicles, satellites and spacecraft vehicles. ... Gross margin increased in 2024 compared to 2023, driven by improved performance on our space vehicle development programs.

claims.claim_text: Moog manufactures motion-control systems for missile systems, tactical and strategic missile steering controls, and missile defense; this is a named market exposure in the Space and Defense segment narrative.
claims.subject: Tactical/strategic missile + missile defense programs
claims.object_value: Missile steering controls and missile defense controls cited as Space and Defense market exposures
claims.source_quote: We manufacture critical defense components and motion-control systems used in defense vehicle platforms, missile systems, naval ships and submarines. ... primary and secondary flight controls and components for military aircraft, tactical and strategic missile steering controls, defense ground vehicle systems including turreted weapon systems

claims.claim_text: Moog's defense market also covers naval ships and submarines (defense vehicle platforms) including 'integrated space vehicles' and 'defense ground vehicle systems including turreted weapon systems'.
claims.subject: Submarines / naval / defense ground vehicles
claims.object_value: Defense ground vehicles + submarines named as Space and Defense segment platforms
claims.source_quote: motion-control systems used in defense vehicle platforms, missile systems, naval ships and submarines.

claims.claim_text: Moog discloses Boeing as a >=10% customer, with combined military/commercial/space-and-defense sales of $396.8M (10%) of FY2025 sales, $417.3M (12%) in FY2024 and $350M (11%) in FY2023. Also discloses that 'a portion of our sales to Boeing is tied to varying levels of government defense spending'.
claims.subject: Boeing customer concentration
claims.source_quote: Sales to Boeing were $396,784, $417,275 and $349,961, or 10%, 12% and 11% of sales, in 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively. ... a portion of our sales to Boeing is tied to varying levels of government defense spending, and a reduction in future U.S. defense spending levels could adversely impact our sales

claims.claim_text: Moog reports a 12-month backlog of $3.0 billion (Sept 27, 2025) and total backlog of $6.0 billion, asserting these are confirmed orders expected to be recognized as revenue. Quality of this backlog depends on Pentagon program continuation.
claims.subject: Total backlog $6.0B / 12-month backlog $3.0B
claims.object_value: $6.0B total backlog, $3.0B 12-month backlog as of Sept 27, 2025
claims.source_quote: Our twelve-month backlog as of September 27, 2025 was $3.0 billion, an increase of 20% compared to September 28, 2024. ... As of September 27, 2025, our total backlog was $6.0 billion, which represents confirmed

claims.claim_text: Moog disclosed in 2023 that the U.S. Air Force announcement to retire the KC-10 aerial refueling tanker caused an impairment charge and an inventory write-down in the Military Aircraft segment, and that Space and Defense recorded impairment on receivables associated with an expected cancellation of a contract.
claims.subject: KC-10 retirement + Space and Defense contract cancellation
claims.object_value: Confirmed historical program-cancellation exposure (KC-10) + acknowledged S&D contract cancellation
claims.source_quote: These charges relate to equipment and inventory that experienced a decline in value due to the U.S. Air Force announcement to retire the KC-10 aerial refueling tanker ... We also recorded impairment charges on receivables in our Space and Defense segment associated with an expected cancellation of a contract.

claims.claim_text: Moog discloses a non-J-Book counterparty/customer disclosure baseline: sales to U.S. Government contracts represented 38% of FY 2025 sales (primarily in Space and Defense and Military Aircraft), 5 largest customers ~31% of sales, aerospace/defense OEM customers 61% of FY 2025 sales.
claims.subject: U.S. Government / OEM customer mix
claims.object_value: U.S. Government 38% / Top 5 ~31% / A&D OEM 61% of FY 2025 sales
claims.source_quote: In 2025, sales under U.S. Government contracts represented 38% of total sales ... Net sales to our five largest customers represented approximately 31% of our 2025 sales. Aerospace and defense OEM customers collectively represented 61% of 2025 sales.

claims.claim_text: Moog maintains a patent portfolio across electrohydraulic, electromechanical, electronics, hydraulics, robotics, wind turbines, vibration control and medical devices, with the medical-device patent sub-portfolio described as significant. (Control claim — non-J-Book.)
claims.subject: Patent portfolio
claims.object_value: Patents across motion control + medical devices; medical-device patents significant
claims.source_quote: We maintain a patent portfolio of issued or pending patents and patent applications worldwide ... The portfolio includes patents that relate to electrohydraulic, electromechanical, electronics, hydraulics, components and methods ... The patent portfolio related to certain medical devices is significant to our position in this market

claims.claim_text: Moog claims that aftermarket sales — primarily to the U.S. Government and commercial airlines — represented 14% of total FY 2025 sales, of which Military Aircraft aftermarket was 23% of Military Aircraft segment sales.
claims.subject: Aftermarket sales mix
claims.object_value: Aftermarket 14% of FY25 sales; Military Aircraft aftermarket 23% of segment
claims.source_quote: In 2025, aftermarket sales accounted for 14% of total sales. ... Aftermarket sales, which represented 23%, 23% and 26% of 2025, 2024 and 2023 sales, respectively, consist of the maintenance, upgrades, spares, repairs and overhauls for military depots and existing fleets.
